questions.question:
Consider the standard second-order system of the form \(\frac{\omega_{n}^{2}}{s^{2}+2 \xi \omega_{n} s+\omega_{n}^{2}}\) with the poles \(p\) and \(p^{\star}\) having negative real parts. The pole locations are also shown in the figure. Now consider two such second-order systems as defined below :

System 1 : \(\omega_{n}=3 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}\) and \(\theta=60^{\circ}\)
System 2 : \(\omega_{n}=1 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}\) and \(\theta=70^{\circ}\)

Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Settling time of System 1 is more than that of System 2.
Settling time of System 2 is more than that of System 1.
Settling times of both the systems are the same.
Settling time cannot be computed from the given information.
questions.explanation:
In system -1
\[\begin{aligned} \xi_{1} & =\cos \theta=\cos 60^{\circ}=0.5 \\ \omega_{n 1} & =3 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}\]
Settling time \(-t_{s 1}=\frac{4}{\xi \omega_{n}}=\frac{4}{0.5 \times 3}=\frac{8}{3}=2.67 \mathrm{sec}\)

In system -2
\[\begin{aligned} \xi_{2} & =\cos \theta_{2}=\cos 70^{\circ} \\ \omega_{n 2} & =1 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}\]
Settling time \(-t_{s 2}=\frac{4}{\xi \omega_{n}}=\frac{4}{\cos 70^{\circ} \times 1}=11.69 \mathrm{sec}\)
So,
\(t_{s 2} > t_{s 1}\)

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: Consider a vector \(\bar{u}=2 \hat{x}+\hat{y}+2 \hat{z}\), where \(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z}\) represent unit vector along the coordinate axes \(x, y, z\) respectively. The directional derivative of the function \(f(x, y, z)=2 \ln (x y)+\ln (y z)+3 \ln (x z)\) at the point \((x, y, z)=(1,1,1)\) in the direction of \(\bar{u}\) is
questions.explanation:
We know that: directional derivative of '\(f\)' at \(P(1,1,1)\) in the direction of \(\vec{a}\) is given by
\[\begin{aligned} \text { Directional derivative } & =\nabla f \cdot \frac{\hat{a}}{|\bar{a}|} \\ \nabla f & =\hat{i} \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}+\hat{j} \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}+\hat{k} \frac{\partial f}{\partial z} \\ \nabla f & =i \frac{5}{x}+j \frac{3}{y}+k \frac{4}{z} \\ (\nabla f)_{(1,1,1)} & =5 i+3 j+4 k \end{aligned}\]
\(\therefore\) Directional derivative \(=\overline{\nabla f} \cdot \frac{\bar{a}}{|\bar{a}|}=(5 i+3 j+4 k) \cdot \frac{(2 i+j+2 k)}{\sqrt{2^{2}+1^{2}+2^{2}}}=\frac{21}{3}=7\)

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question:
The input \(x(t)\) and the output \(y(t)\) of a system are related as

\(y(t)=e^{-t} \int_{-\infty}^{t} e^{\tau} x(\tau) d \tau, \quad-\infty \lt t \lt \infty\)

The system is
questions.explanation:
System will follow law of superposition. Therefore, system will be linear.
Time-invariance check:
\(y\left(t-t_{0}\right)=e^{-\left(t-t_{0}\right)} \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{\tau} \cdot x(\tau) d \tau\)
For input \(x\left(t-t_{0}\right)\), output will be
\(y(t)=e^{-t} \int_{-\infty}^{t} e^{\tau} \cdot x\left(\tau-t_{0}\right) d \tau\)
Put \(\tau-t_{o}=k\), then \(d \tau=d k\) and for \(\tau=t, k=t-t_{0}\)
\[\begin{aligned} & =e^{-t} \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{k+t_{0}} \cdot x(k) d k \\ & =e^{-t} \times e^{t o} \times \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{k} \cdot x(k) d k=e^{-\left(t-t_{0}\right)} \times \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{k} \cdot x(k) d k \\ & =e^{-\left(t-t_{0}\right)} \times \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{\tau} \cdot x(\tau) d \tau \end{aligned}\]
Since,
\(y(t)=y\left(t-t_{0}\right)\)
So, the system is time-invariant.

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question:
Consider the discrete-time system \(T_{1}\) and \(T_{2}\) defined as follows:

\[\begin{aligned} & \left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n]=x[0]+x[1]+\ldots+x[n] \\ & \left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n]=x[0]+\frac{1}{2} x[1]+\cdots+\frac{1}{2^{n}} x[n] \end{aligned}\]

Which one of the following statement is true?
options: \(T_{1}\) is BIBO stable but \(T_{2}\) is not BIBO stable.
\(T_{1}\) is not BIBO stable but \(T_{2}\) is BIBO stable.
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} \left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n] & =x[0]+x[1]+\ldots+x[n] \\ \left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n]^{-} & =\sum_{K=0}^{n} x[K] \end{aligned}\]
Let,
\[\begin{aligned} x[K] & =u[K] \\ \mid x[K] & =|u[K]| \\ \left|\left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n]\right| & =\left|\sum_{K=0}^{n} u[K]\right|=\sum_{K=0}^{n} 1=n \end{aligned}\]
\(\mid\left[\left.T_{1} x(n)\right|_{n=\infty}=\infty\right.\) system is not BIBO stable
\[\begin{aligned} \left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n] & =x[0]+\frac{1}{2} x[1]+\cdots+\frac{1}{2^{n}} x[n] \\ & =\sum_{K=0}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K} x(K) \end{aligned}\]
Let,
\[\begin{aligned} x(K) & =u[K] \\ |x[K]| & =\mid u[K] \\ \left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n] & =\sum_{K=0}^{n}\left|\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K} u(K)\right| \\ \left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n] & =\sum_{K=0}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K} \\ \mid\left[\left.T_{2} x(n)\right|_{n=\infty}\right. & =\sum_{K=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K}=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2}}=2 \text { stable } \end{aligned}\]
\(T_{1}\) is not BIBO stable but \(T_{2}\) is \(\mathrm{BIBO}\) stable.

questions.question: If the Z-transform of a finite-duration discrete-time signal \(x[n]\) is \(X(z)\), then the \(Z\)-transform of the signal \(y[n]=x[2 n]\) is
questions.explanation:
\(Y(z)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} y(n) z^{-n}=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} x(2 n) z^{-n}\)
Let
\(2 n=m\)
then
\[\begin{aligned} n & =\frac{m}{2}=\sum_{m=\text { even-int. }} x(m) z^{-m / 2} \\ & =\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}\left[\frac{x(m)+(-1)^{m} x(m)}{2}\right] z^{-m / 2} \end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} x(m) z^{-m / 2}+\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}(-1)^{m} x(m) z^{-m / 2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} x(m)\left(z^{1 / 2}\right)^{-m}+\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} x(m)\left(-z^{1 / 2}\right)^{m}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[x\left(z^{1 / 2}\right)+x\left(-z^{1 / 2}\right)\right] \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question: A 3-phase. \(11 \mathrm{kV} .10\) MVA synchronous generator is connected to an inductive load of power factor \((\sqrt{3} / 2)\) via a lossless line with a per-phase inductive reactance of \(5 \Omega\). The per-phase synchronous reactance of the generator is \(30 \Omega\) with negligible armature resistance. If the generator is producing the rated current at the rated voltage, then the power factor at the terminal of the generator is
questions.explanation:
\(\mathrm{pF}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=30^{\circ} \text { lagging }\)
\[\begin{aligned} E & =\sqrt{(V \cos 30+I R)^2+\left(V \sin 30^{\circ}+I X\right)^2} \\ E & =\sqrt{(V \cos +I R)^2+(V \sin +I X)} \\ \frac{11 \mathrm{~K}}{\sqrt{3}} & =\sqrt{\left(V \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{V}{2}+524.86(5)\right)^2} \\ \left(\frac{11 \mathrm{~K}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 & =V^2 \cdot \frac{3}{4}+\left(\frac{V}{2}+2624.319\right)^2 \\ \left(\frac{11 \mathrm{~K}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 & =\frac{3}{4} V^2+\frac{V^2}{4}+2624.319 \mathrm{~V}+2624.319^2 \\ V_t & =4618.105 \mathrm{~V} \\ (I Z)^2 & =E^2+V^2-2 E V \cos \delta \\ (2624.319)^2 & =\left(\frac{11 \mathrm{~K}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2+(4618.105)^2-2\left(\frac{11 \mathrm{~K}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)(4618.105) \cos \delta \\ \delta & =20.96 \\ \mathrm{pF} & =\cos (20.96+30)=0.629 \text { lagging } \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: In the \((x, y, z)\) coordinate system, three point-charges \(Q, Q\) and \(\alpha Q\) are located in free space at \((-1,0,0),(1,0,0)\) and \((0,-1,0)\) respectively. The value of \(\alpha\) for the electric field to be zero at \((0,0.5,0)\) is _____ (rounded off to 1 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
From the figure,
\(\left.\bar{E}_{n e t}=\bar{E}_{1 y}+\bar{E}_{2 y}+\bar{E}_{\alpha Q}=0 \text { [as per question }\right]\)
Here,
\(\bar{E}_{1 y}=\bar{E}_{2 y}=\bar{E}_{Q} \text { (say) }\)
\(\therefore \quad \bar{E}_{n e t}=\left.2 E\right|_{Q}+\left.2 E\right|_{\alpha Q}=0\)
Now,
\(\left.\bar{E}\right|_{Q}=\frac{k Q}{\left[\sqrt{1+0.5^{2}}\right]^{2}} \sin \theta \hat{a}_{y} ; \quad k=\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{o}}\)
\(\left.\Rightarrow \quad \bar{E}\right|_{Q}=\frac{k Q}{1.25} \times \frac{0.5}{\sqrt{1+0.5^{2}}} \hat{a}_{y}=0.357 k Q \hat{a}_{y}\)
Also, \(\left.\quad \bar{E}\right|_{\alpha Q}=\frac{k(\alpha Q)}{(1.5)^{2}} \hat{a}_{y}=0.444 k(\alpha Q) \hat{a}_{y}\)
Hence, \(\quad \bar{E}_{n e t}=2 \times 0.357 k Q \hat{a}_{y}+0.444 k(\alpha Q) \hat{a}_{y}=0\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad 0.715 \mathrm{kQ}=-0.444 \mathrm{k}(\alpha Q)\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad \alpha=\frac{-0.715}{0.444}=-1.61\)
\(\therefore \quad \alpha=-1.61\)
